newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust buys NationsBank trust business.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust buys NationsBank trust business.

text.p: Bankers Trust New York Corp. said on Friday it has agreed to acquire NationsBank Corp.'s $1.33 billion-asset institutional trust business.
Terms of the definitive agreement were not disclosed, but Bankers Trust said the deal would have no material effect on its earnings.
An industry source said a final price is typically not determined until some time after the deal closes, based on how much of the accounts are retained by the buyer.
The deal involves NationsBank's 465 master trust and custody accounts, allowing the company to focus on its investment and investment-related businesses, it said.

Bankers Trust Chairman Frank Newman said in a statement that the acquisition -- which boosts its assets under custody to nearly $2 trillion -- "fits our goal of expanding our institutional trust business and will allow us to further leverage our technology and custody infrastructure."
The deal, still subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close before July.
Bankers Trust said it plans to open additional offices in such cities as Dallas, St. Louis and Kansas City to serve some of its newly acquired clients.

"This continues our stated strategy of expanding our presence across the United States, begun last year with the addition of personnel to our Chicago and San Francisco offices," said Timothy Keaney, head of Bankers Trust's global retirement services.

"This confirms their recent pronouncements that their processing division is not for sale and that they would more likely embellish it," said George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison, referring to Bankers Trust.

Salem said one of the attractions of NationsBank's trust business was its growth. For Bankers Trust in particular, he said, the business "provides stability to an income statement which is pretty volatile now."
Announcing first-quarter earnings last week, Bankers Trust said client processing services contributed net income of $13 million, down from $18 million in the year-ago period.

Overall net income grew to $169 million from $138 million a year ago, due to higher operations costs and growth in staff expense. Revenues in the client processing business rose $14 million to $196 million.
Bankers Trust spokesman Alan Hanson said the company spends $500 million a year on technology, with about one-third going to global trust and custody and cash management.
Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Raphael Soifer said Bankers Trust expects to complete work on a "very expensive" global custody system by the end of 1997.

Analysts said companies like Bankers Trust, State Street Corp. and Bank of New York Co. Inc. that have committed themselves to the business and the spending that goes with it will benefit from economies of scale as other players withdraw.

Bankers Trust, which has been providing institutional trust services since its founding in 1903, is the fourth-largest custody provider worldwide, with a subcustodial network that covers more than 60 countries.
Bankers Trust's stock fell 75 cents to $77.125, while NationsBank rose 37.5 cents to $57.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
